text:
Note: my workspace listing commands returned no output, so I could not read any run records, metrics.json files or notes. The answers below come from the script, the measurements you gave and arithmetic. Where provenance can only be settled by a run or a log, I say so.

QUESTIONS, aimed at the weakest links first:

Q1: Does the 21.24M baseline parameter count show which script the measurements came from? | decides: treat the step-26/51/100 numbers as this MLA script's own baseline vs. re-measure them on this script before any comparison
A1: No. The two models are parameter-matched to within about 1k, so the count fits both. MHA at d_ff=1024 has 4×147,456 attention + 3×384×1024 MLP + 768 norms = 1,770,240 per block, 21,243,264 total. This MLA script at d_ff=1077 has 1,770,160 per block, 21,242,304 total. d_ff=1077 is evidently the parameter-matching choice: the 53 extra FFN columns (61,056) offset the MLA saving of 61,184.

Q2: Can the loss baselines (7.0622 at step 26, 6.5902 at step 51, recall 4.475 at step 100) be compared with a 45-step smoke run? | decides: KILL measured against those numbers vs. KILL measured against a fresh baseline run with an identical `--smoke-steps 45`
A2: No. `--smoke-steps N` sets `total_steps = N`, and `lr_mult` scales with it. A 45-step run has warmup of 1 step and cooldown from step 31. The full run (1525 steps) has a 30-step warmup and no cooldown before step 1067. A step-100 number can only come from a run of at least 100 steps, so it used a different schedule from the 45-step test. The step-40-to-45 KILL needs a baseline run of this script with `--smoke-steps 45`, on the same seeds.

Q3: Which script produced the layer-0 gradient, attention-mass and recall/rare measurements? | decides: trust the layer-0 anomaly and the absence of a sink as properties of this MLA + 4-stream model vs. re-probe them
A3: Unknown; I found no logs. The first-token mass needs explicit attention probabilities, since SDPA does not return them. In this script the probe would have to rebuild `cat(qc_norm, qr)·cat(k_norm, kr)` with the 96-dim scale; an MHA probe would not carry over. The layer-0 gradient spike could also come from the 4-stream embedding broadcast, which the MHA baseline does not have.

Q4: Does this MLA + mHC script already trail the pooled baseline mean on the exam? | decides: aim the gate at beating the baseline by 0.005 vs. treat the gate first as recovering an MLA deficit (or drop MLA and gate an MHA key/value path)
A4: Unknown. No exam loss for this script is given, and the pooled baseline mean is not given either. Published evidence at small scale is mixed: MLA without RoPE trailed MHA by 3–5% at 30M (https://arxiv.org/html/2506.09342v2). The decoupled-rotary variant used here is the one that avoided rank collapse (https://arxiv.org/html/2507.09394v1), but that paper gives no matched loss figure that I can cite.

Q5: Is the C7 comparator the MHA nano-GPT2 pool or this script? | decides: 3 seeds of this script as a control arm vs. relying only on the harness pool
A5: The pool is the harness baseline, which the docstring names as nano-GPT2 MHA (nano_specs.md section A). Even so, this script's own 3-seed exam is needed to separate "the gate helps" from "MLA/mHC hurt". If the gate's gain is smaller than an existing MLA deficit, the candidate fails C7 even though the gate works.

Q6: Is L1's "gate CV above 0.1" test informative? | decides: keep the CV metric vs. replace it with a change-from-init or a per-token selectivity metric
A6: No; it passes trivially at initialisation. The gate input is the normed read, so gate pre-activations have std ≈ 0.02·√384 ≈ 0.39. silu(z) for z ~ N(0, 0.39²) has mean ≈ 0.04 and std ≈ 0.2, which gives a CV of several units before any training. A useful check is the top-16 energy share against the ungated latent and against the gate's own value at step 0, or the gate's correlation with token identity.

Q7: Does the gate threaten C4 (VRAM or step time)? | decides: run a full VRAM rung vs. a 3-step smoke being enough
A7: It is unlikely to. At micro-batch 4 the extra activations are about 3 × 4·1024·128 × 2 bytes ≈ 3 MB per layer, about 38 MB over 12 layers. The extra matmul is 384×128 per token, about 2% of block FLOPs. The 3-step smoke is enough, but the step-time ratio must be measured against the baseline, not against this script.

Q8: Does the product start near the old linear code, as L3 hopes? | decides: plain gate init vs. a gate bias or offset init (silu(g+c)) that starts the latent close to the linear code
A8: No. At std 0.02 the latent ≈ RMSNorm(compress(x) ⊙ (gate(x)/2 + gate(x)²/4)), a roughly bilinear code with random signs per channel. RMSNorm restores its scale, so the result is not the old linear image. If L3's early-loss check fails, an offset of about +2 on the gate pre-activation (silu ≈ linear-scaled, near-constant) is the fallback; with `bias=False` that needs an extra parameter of 128 values.

KNOWN:
- 21.24M non-embedding matches both MHA at d_ff=1024 (21,243,264) and this MLA at d_ff=1077 (21,242,304), so the count does not show provenance [belief]
- d_ff=1077 offsets the MLA attention saving of 61,184 with 61,056 extra FFN params [script]
- Gate adds 49,152 params/layer and 589,824 total, giving about 21.83M against a cap of about 23.37M [measured]
- Plug-in: `self.gate = nn.Linear(cfg.d_model, 128, bias=False)`; `kv = self.expand(self.latent_norm(self.compress(x) * F.silu(self.gate(x))))`. The gate is 2-D, so Muon picks it up and `_init` gives std 0.02 [script]
- `--smoke-steps N` compresses the LR schedule to N steps: warmup 1, cooldown from step 31 at N=45. Full run: 1525 steps, warmup 30, cooldown from step 1067 [script]
- The baseline step-26/51/100 numbers come from a run of at least 100 steps, with a schedule unknown to me [measured]
- Gate pre-activation std at init is about 0.39 on the normed read, so the silu output CV across tokens is well above 0.1 before training [belief]
- Extra activation memory about 38 MB; extra FLOPs about 2% of a block [belief]
- The decoupled rotary path (32 dims, shared across heads) bypasses the latent, so the gate does not touch position (https://arxiv.org/html/2507.09394v1) [web]
- Recall tokens are 13% of targets (4.475 vs 6.704); rare tokens 12% (11.613), all at step 100 [measured]
- The C7 comparator is the harness's pooled baseline mean, which the docstring describes as the MHA nano-GPT2 [script]

ASSUMES:
- The measured baselines belong to this MLA + 4-stream script, not to the MHA nano-GPT2.
- This script is at least level with the pooled baseline, so a gate gain of about 0.01 translates into a C7 pass.
- A 45-step matched smoke predicts the 1525-step exam ranking.
- The 128-dim latent is the binding bottleneck, rather than the shared 32-dim rotary key or the 4-stream read.
- Gating belongs before the latent norm, on the input side, rather than after the expansion.
- K and V should share one gated code.
- All 12 layers benefit equally.

NEW IDEAS:

SLOT: drop
IDEA: Separate K and V gates
MECHANISM: Drop "K and V share one gated code". Keep one ungated linear latent for K, and gate only the V half of the expansion with silu(W_g c), so retrieval geometry stays linear while the content read out is selected per token.
PREDICTION: Recall-token loss falls more than all-token loss; attention entropy stays unchanged compared with the shared-gate version.
TEST: 45-step matched smoke against this script and against the shared gate; compare recall-token loss at step 45.
SOURCE: own
PART: Sequence mixing: latent KV compression and expansion

SLOT: strengthen
IDEA: Gate offset init to the linear code
MECHANISM: Initialise the gate pre-activation with a learned per-channel offset of +2, so silu(gate) is roughly a constant 1.76 at step 0 and the latent starts as the old linear code. Selectivity then grows only where gradients ask for it.
PREDICTION: Step-26 loss matches the baseline within 0.01, with the gate gain appearing after warmup.
TEST: Loss at steps 26/51 with matched `--smoke-steps`, compared with the plain gate.
SOURCE: own
PART: Sequence mixing: latent KV compression and expansion

SLOT: specialise
IDEA: Gate only layers 0–3
MECHANISM: Apply the gate only in the four lowest layers, where token-identity-conditional features matter most and the layer-0 gradient spike sits. That uses 197k params instead of 590k.
PREDICTION: At least 70% of the full-gate gain, plus a lower layer-0 gradient norm.
TEST: Matched smoke; compare the layer-0 attention gradient (0.2406 baseline) and loss at step 45.
SOURCE: own
PART: Sequence mixing: latent KV compression and expansion

SLOT: port
IDEA: Gated stream read
MECHANISM: Replace the static `read_logits` softmax with a token-conditional sigmoid gate over the 4 streams, computed from the stream-mean, so each token chooses which residual stream feeds attention.
PREDICTION: Read weights diverge across tokens; loss down at step 100 with fewer than 4k extra params.
TEST: Smoke run; measure the per-token read-weight variance and loss against this script.
SOURCE: own
PART: Residual stream: hyper-connection mixing

SLOT: combine
IDEA: Gated latent + gated attention output
MECHANISM: Combine the latent gate with the known per-head sigmoid output gate on the SDPA result (Qiu et al. 2025, gated attention), so selection happens both before keys and values are coded and after retrieval.
PREDICTION: The gains roughly add up; attention-output norm becomes more uneven across heads.
TEST: 2×2 matched smoke (neither, latent gate, output gate, both) at 45 steps.
SOURCE: https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.06708
PART: Sequence mixing: latent KV compression and expansion

SLOT: other
IDEA: Latent as top-k sparse code
MECHANISM: Replace the RMSNorm'd dense latent with a hard top-32-of-128 sparse code (straight-through gradient), forcing token-conditional channel selection outright instead of hoping a silu gate learns it.
PREDICTION: The top-16 energy share rises to above 0.8; recall-token loss falls; early loss may rise.
TEST: Step-26/51 loss in a matched smoke.
SOURCE: own
PART: Sequence mixing: latent KV compression and expansion
KIND: leap
BREAKS: The latent is a dense code that every head reads in full.
KILL: Step-26 loss more than 0.05 above this script's matched baseline on all 3 seeds.

OPEN:
- Exam val loss of this MLA script over 3 seeds against the pooled baseline mean | build: yes | decides: gate as a gain on top of the baseline vs. dropping MLA and gating an MHA key/value path
- Which script and schedule produced 7.0622 / 6.5902 / 4.475 / 11.613 | build: yes | decides: reuse those numbers vs. re-measure them on this script
- Seed-to-seed std of the exam loss for this script | build: yes | decides: 3 seeds vs. 5 or more seeds for p < 0.01
- Whether the layer-0 gradient spike comes from the 4-stream broadcast | build: yes | decides: gate all layers vs. layers 1 and up only
- Whether 45-step rankings carry over to 1525 steps | build: yes | decides: 45-step KILL vs. 200-step KILL
- Gate placement: before the latent norm vs. after the expansion | build: yes | decides: input-side gate vs. gated expansion (the variant)

LINK STATUS:
- L1: open | The CV > 0.1 threshold is met at init by construction (pre-activation std about 0.39), so it cannot refute; the top-16 share against the ungated latent at a matched step is still unmeasured.
- L2: open | The 4.475 recall baseline has unknown provenance and schedule; it needs re-measuring on this script at a matched `--smoke-steps`.
- L3: open | The step-26/51 baselines are not schedule-matched to a 45-step smoke, and the product does not start as the linear code, so the early-loss risk is real.
- L4: open | The 11.613 rare-token baseline has the same provenance problem as L2.
- L5: open | Neither this script's exam loss nor the pooled baseline mean is known, so it is undetermined whether the gate must also make up an MLA/mHC deficit.
